control_name: Key Fact Statement (KFS) disclosure at sanction
description: KFS with APR issued to every digital-loan borrower before disbursal.
Documented due diligence on every Lending Service Provider and Digital Lending App.
Borrower can exit within the cooling-off window without penalty (only APR).
Loan funds move bank-to-borrower with no LSP pass-through / pool account.
DLG exposure kept within the 5% regulatory cap per portfolio.
Recovery calls only 08:00-19:00, agents trained and logged.
Complaints resolved within regulatory TAT; GRO/Nodal officer published.
DLA collects only need-based data with explicit, auditable consent.
Identity/address verification and risk profiling at account opening.
Video-KYC sessions live, geo-tagged, and reviewed for tampering.
Re-KYC performed on schedule by customer risk band.
Every customer classified low/medium/high and reviewed periodically.
Customers and counterparties screened against sanction/PEP lists.
Suspicious transactions reported within the prescribed timeline.
Wallet load/balance kept within PPI-tier limits by KYC status.
Daily reconciliation of nodal/escrow balances against customer liability.
Failed/declined UPI debits auto-reversed within the mandated window.
Per-scenario TAT tracked; compensation paid on breach.
Merchant KYC, category-risk review and ongoing monitoring.
Card disputes and chargebacks handled within network SLAs.
Cardholder data environment maintained to PCI-DSS.
All payment data stored only within India.
Personal data used only for consented, stated purposes.
Data retained only for the defined period, then purged.
Role-based access reviewed; least-privilege enforced across systems.
Vulnerability assessment and pen-testing on schedule with closure.
Cyber incidents reported to RBI/CERT-In within the 6-hour window.
DR/BCP plan maintained and drills conducted periodically.
Returns filed accurately and on time with maker-checker.
New/changed reporting formats implemented before effective date.
Outsourcing contracts carry audit rights and exit/BCP clauses.
Material vendors and LSPs risk-assessed at defined frequency.
Transaction fraud rules tuned; alerts triaged within SLA.
Frauds reported to RBI in the prescribed format and timeline.
Regulatory changes assessed and productised via change control.

control_name: Penal charges vs penal interest segregation
description: Penal charges levied as charges (not capitalised interest) and disclosed.

control_name: Tokenisation / de-tokenisation restricted to card network
description: Only the authorised card network performs tokenisation and de-tokenisation; PAN recovery is feasible for the network alone.
Cryptographic safeguards ensure PAN cannot be derived from a token or vice versa; token generation integrity monitored continuously.
Every tokenisation and de-tokenisation request is logged by the card network and retrievable on demand.
Token requestors are contractually barred from storing PAN or any other card detail, verified by attestation and scan.
Card network certifies token requestor systems, app security, authorised-access features, onboarding, provisioning, storage and transaction processing.

control_name: Payment-chain entity certification for tokenised processing
description: Issuers, acquirers and service providers in the transaction chain are certified for changes made to process tokenised transactions.

control_name: Explicit AFA consent at card registration
description: Card registration on a token requestor app requires explicit customer consent through AFA - never a pre-ticked or default selection.
Customers can register or de-register a card for each use case (contactless, QR, in-app) independently.

control_name: Customer-set per-transaction and daily token limits
description: Customers can set and modify per-transaction and daily limits for tokenised card transactions.
Daily / weekly / monthly velocity thresholds applied to tokenised card transactions by issuer and network.

control_name: Secure token and key storage on identified device
description: Tokens and associated keys are stored in a secure element / TEE on the identified device after successful registration.
Customers can report loss of an identified device through any channel; tokens and keys are de-activated immediately.
A defined dispute-resolution process covers tokenised card transactions end to end.
Each transaction request is verified to have originated from the registered identified device before authorisation.
Monitoring detects malfunction, anomaly, suspicious behaviour or unauthorised activity in the tokenisation process and alerts all stakeholders.
Issuer decides, on risk perception, which of its card ranges may be registered by a token requestor; rules reviewed periodically.

control_name: Annual CERT-In empanelled tokenisation system audit
description: System and security audit of all entities involved in tokenisation, at least annually, by CERT-In empanelled auditors.

control_name: Tokenisation audit report submission to RBI
description: Audit report, with auditor comments on deviations from Annex 1 and the compliance thereto, furnished to the Reserve Bank.
Annex 2 return on token requestors, use cases, cards registered and transaction volumes filed with CGM DPSS by the 10th of each month.
No charge of any kind is recovered from the customer for availing the tokenisation service.
